transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
i was back at my old school, late for an exam. walking down that long green corridor with lockers all along it.

that long green corridor is such a specific feeling. late for an exam too.

was anyone else around, or just you walking?
just me. the corridor was empty.

empty school, just your shoes on the floor probably. that kind of quiet.

do you remember what happened next?
at the end of the corridor there was a wooden door with a small round window. i looked through and the classroom was full of students but none of them had faces.

oh. that's eerie.

did it feel like they were waiting for you?
kind of. they were all at their desks, rows of them, just sitting there. no faces, just smooth skin.

smooth skin where faces should be... that's the kind of image that stays with you.

did you go through the door or stay where you were?
i went in. my old maths teacher was there, mrs okafor, in her red cardigan, writing numbers on the board.

mrs okafor in her red cardigan. you really see her.

was she facing the board the whole time?
at first yes. then she turned round and she was a tall grey heron, still wearing the red cardigan.

a heron in a red cardigan, but still her, somehow.

how did you feel seeing her like that?
it wasn't scary really. she just walked to the window on those long legs and flew out.

that's so strange... just walked over and flew out, like it was nothing.

did anyone else in the room react?
i don't remember them reacting. then somehow i was flying next to her over the town.

you were flying right next to her over the town...

that shift from being in the room to being in the air... did it feel sudden to you?
yeah it was sudden. one moment she flew out and then i was out there with her.

that's how dreams do it. no big transition, you're just... there.

what could you see below you, over the town?
i could see the school roof far below and the river shining. i felt very small, like a sparrow.

small like a sparrow but flying with a heron... that's a whole feeling.

were you flying with wings, or was it more like gliding on the air?
more like gliding i think. just in the air with her.

just in the air with her, above the school roof and the river.

what happened after that?
that's where it ended. i woke up.

that's a clean place for it to end. like you lifted right out of the dream.

when you look back at it now, is there one moment that stays with you more than the rest?
probably the heron in the red cardigan. that's the part i keep seeing.

she's the heart of it. a tall grey heron in a red cardigan, writing numbers one minute, flying next to you the next.

did anything about her or the cardigan stay with you in your mind's eye?
the cardigan was just plain red. no buttons or anything. and she was really tall.

just plain red, no buttons... and her tallness is part of it too.

was there anything in the dream that you felt mattered especially, or did it all feel kind of loose and passing?
it felt loose mostly, but the corridor felt important too. that long green corridor.

so you were back at your old school, late for an exam, walking down that long green corridor with lockers, empty. at the end, a wooden door with a round window, and you looked through to a classroom full of students with no faces, just smooth skin. you went in, mrs okafor in her red cardigan was writing on the board, then she turned into a tall grey heron, still wearing the cardigan, walked to the window on long legs and flew out. then suddenly you were flying next to her over the town, gliding, seeing the school roof far below and the river shining, feeling small like a sparrow. it ended there. the corridor felt important too, and the heron in the red cardigan is what stays with you.

did i get that right? or missed anything?
yeah that's right. you got it.
would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i would.

there are a few ways it could be drawn.

it could be an old woodcut print, like a memory from long ago with solid certainty. or soft watercolour, seen through tired eyes with colours running. or a tin-type photograph, an artifact from another time with a metallic sheen. or a photograph, exactly like your own eyes with impossible things taken as normal. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
out of those, soft watercolour feels closest, like colours running.

ok, soft watercolour then. i'll start with the classroom.

i picture it like this: desks in rows, a blackboard with numbers, a window. classroom light, ordinary. those are my guesses. does anything feel different, or shall i leave it to you?
that sounds right. go with your guess.

ok, i'm sketching the classroom and mrs okafor and the long green corridor and the town from above now, it'll appear on the right. just that for now, nothing else.

as you are, maybe with a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
as me, ordinary. nothing special.
so just as you, ordinary, nothing special. did i get that right, or is there anything different?
yeah, that's right.
ok. i'm sketching you now. everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
i can see them. the corridor looks right, and the heron in the red cardigan is right too.

i'm glad those feel right.

does the whole picture look the way you remember it?
yes, it looks like the dream. the school roof and the river are there. feels right.
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the last. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
alright. i can see the first ones. the corridor and the classroom look how i remember.

good, those two feel right to you.

and the one with the school roof far below and the river shining, does that look like your dream too?
yeah, that one looks right too. the river is shining like it did.
that one feels right too. the next moments are being drawn now, they'll appear on the right soon.
ok. i can see another one now. it looks like when she turned round as the heron. that fits.

the heron turning round...

does it look the way you remember it?
it does, the red cardigan is right too.
the red cardigan being right feels good. more moments are being drawn now, they'll appear on the right soon.
ok.
ok. i'll keep drawing the rest, they'll appear on the right as each one is ready.
i see five now. the one of me flying with her is there. it looks right.

the flying one with her, over the roof and the river, that's good it feels right.

once you've had a look at that one, the next moments will be drawn in order. does the one of you entering the classroom, with mrs okafor at the board in her red cardigan, look the way you remember?
yeah, that one is there too. mrs okafor at the board in the red cardigan, the students with no faces at their desks. it's right.

nice, that one feels right to you.

the rest are still being drawn, they'll appear on the right soon.
